writeup: TIC 59453672 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 8.357922 days and a primary eclipse depth of 2.15 percent. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected the eclipse signal with high statistical significance (signal-to-noise ratio of 239.0), and pixel-level imaging confirmed a peak signal-to-noise of 7.6 with a centroid offset of 10.2 arcseconds from the target. No secondary eclipse was detected. A notable data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true period is double the initially measured value - a pattern consistent with eclipsing binary behavior. While the pipeline's machine-learning model rates this candidate at 0.83 confidence, the alternating eclipse-depth pattern represents an open question requiring further investigation.
